title: The Next Chapter of Africa-China Climate Cooperation
author: Yike Fu
text:
A solar power station near Clanwilliam in the Western Cape Province of South Africa.
Credit: Shutterstock
Nearly five years have passed since the adoption of the Declaration on China-Africa Cooperation on Combating Climate Change at the Eighth Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC 8) in 2021. Since then, discussions have often centered on simple indicators to reflect on the progress made – for example, the number of projects announced, the size of new investments, and the scale of renewable energy commitments.At first glance, Development Reimagined’s China-Africa Climate Action Tracker provides just this. The tracker captures 246 publicly announced climate actions across 50 African countries between 2022 and the first half of 2026, including nearly 49 GW of renewable energy in the development pipeline, clean technologies, clean transportation, and, more recently, critical minerals. However, while these results are important,  they capture only part of a partnership that has evolved significantly over the past five years.[...]
